memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish; he took up positions against it and attacked it. The Lord gave Lachish into Israel's hands, and Joshua took it on the second day. The city and everyone in it he put to the sword, just as he had done to Libnah. Meanwhile, Horam king of Gezer had come up to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his army — until no survivors were left. — Josh 10:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel presses on to Lachish, a small detail stands out: "Joshua took it on the second day." Lachish did not fall as quickly as some of the other cities. It took an extra day, a little more perseverance, before the victory came. Not every battle is won at the first attempt. Some require us to keep going a second day, to persist when the breakthrough does not come immediately.

This is a quiet but valuable encouragement. We can grow discouraged when a struggle does not resolve on the first try. We pray, we make an effort, and nothing seems to happen, so we are tempted to give up, concluding that God is not going to act. But sometimes the victory simply comes on "the second day." Perseverance matters. God's timing is not always our timing, and He often works through our steady persistence rather than instant results.

Notice, too, the arrival of Horam king of Gezer, coming to help Lachish. Just when one battle was underway, another enemy appeared. Yet he too was defeated. Sometimes opposition seems to multiply, with new challenges arriving before the old ones are finished. But no combination of enemies could stand against the God who fought for Israel.

The lesson is to keep going and keep trusting. Scripture urges us, "Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up" (Gal 6:9). Whether the victory comes on the first day or the second, whether one enemy stands against us or several, our God is faithful. We are called simply to persevere, trusting the One who gives the victory in His time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you give up too easily when a struggle isn't resolved on the first attempt?
2. Where might God be calling you to persevere to "the second day"?
3. How does trusting God's timing help you keep going when results are delayed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when the victory does not come at once, help me persevere and not grow weary. Teach me to trust Your timing, knowing You are faithful to give the victory. Amen.
